elements.content: Grammar focus: Mandative & Formulaic Subjunctive.

Use the base verb, never a tense form, after the that-clause: that he be, that she leave, that it not proceed. In British English the indicative is acceptable in informal writing (that she is on time), but the subjunctive is expected in formal and academic registers. Keep not before the base verb in the negative.

suggest / recommend that — advice, formal: the doctor suggested that he rest
demand / insist / request that — pressure, formal: they demanded that he leave
it is essential / vital that — necessity: it is essential that she be on time
it is imperative / crucial that — urgency: it is imperative that the file be kept
negative subjunctive — not before the base verb: we recommend that it not proceed
fixed formulas — set expressions: be that as it may, suffice it to say
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Complete: 'It is vital that the file ___ kept.'
2. Complete: 'They insisted that the meeting ___ recorded.'
3. Which verb takes the subjunctive?
Read and listen: three examples in context.

They demanded that he resign. — Base verb after demand. (No -s, no tense change.)
It is vital that the file be kept. — Base be after an adjective of necessity. (Be, not is.)
The board recommended that the plan be revised. — Recommendation in formal register. (Same pattern after recommend.)
What do you observe?

The mandative subjunctive uses the base form of the verb after verbs of demand and suggestion (suggest, demand, insist, propose, recommend, request, urge) and after adjectives of necessity (essential, vital, crucial, imperative, necessary). The base form does not change with person or tense: it is essential that she be on time, they demanded that he leave, we insist that the report be published.
1. Which form follows 'It is essential that she ___'?
2. Does the subjunctive change in the past?
options: No: it was essential that she be there.
Yes: it was essential that she was there.

elements.content: State the rule in one sentence, without looking at the table.
Freer production: Can defend a complex position, nuance reservations, and chair executive debates fluently

Success criteria:
- I can use the base verb after demand, suggest and recommend.
- I can use be after adjectives of necessity.
- I can put not before the base verb in the negative.
Role play: put your position in ninety seconds; your partner notes every use of the target structure.
Frequent errors and correction:

❌ It is essential that she is on time in a formal recommendation (indicative in a mandatory clause) → ✅ It is essential that she be on time
❌ They demanded that he leaves (third person -s in the subjunctive) → ✅ They demanded that he leave
Correct these sentences: say what is wrong, then give the right version.
Acceptable variants:

The panel recommends that the report be published in full.
It is vital that the data be checked twice.
They insisted that the meeting not be recorded.
